Tim Cook visited Apple’s Battersea campus in London this week, mingling with King Charles as part of the company’s new partnership with The King’s Trust.

At Apple’s Battersea headquarters, Cook also sat down with The Independent for an in-depth interview on the partnership and his first month as Apple’s executive chairman.

Cook stepped down as Apple CEO last month, passing the torch to John Ternus. In this week’s interview, Cook outlined that the transition “actually started years ago.”

Ternus’s tenure as CEO began with the launch of the iPhone Duo, which Cook said was fully planned. “I wanted John to have some wind at his back,” Cook explained. “And the wind at Apple is very much based on the product cycle.”

Cook also emphasized that he’s focused on “worldwide policy” as Apple’s executive chairman, noting the “incredible level of trust” between him and Ternus. While Cook is helping Ternus in “any way he sees fit,” he makes it clear he’s “not meddling.”

What kind of advice has Cook given Ternus? “Don’t mimic me.” You can read the full interview over at The Independent. It includes a great discussion on Apple’s new partnership with The King’s Trust.
